subject: [RFC PATCH v2 00/18] mm: read the page cache without folio references

reviews.author: Kiryl (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about memory safety when reading from the page cache without taking a reference, explaining that adding PG_rcu_free flag would allow readers to safely access folios marked for deferred free during an RCU grace period.
reviews.raw_body:
From: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

Reading a page cache folio without taking a reference would keep CPUs
that read the same file from bouncing its refcount.  But without a
reference the folio can be freed, and its memory reused, while the
reader copies from it.

Add PG_rcu_free: the free of a folio with the flag waits for an RCU
grace period.  A reader that saw the flag under rcu_read_lock(), and
then still found the folio where it looked, can read it until
rcu_read_unlock().  A split copies the flag, as such a reader may still
be reading the new folios.

The folios wait on per-CPU lists, one grace period in flight per CPU:
call_rcu() per folio would queue a callback for every folio of a
truncated file.  A work, which can reschedule, frees each batch.
Reclaim depends on these frees, so the workqueue is WQ_MEM_RECLAIM.

The flag is 64-bit only (CONFIG_PAGE_RCU_FREE): page flags are scarce
on 32-bit, and the contention this avoids is a problem of large
machines.  It is off on PREEMPT_RT, where expedited grace periods are
normal ones, so the waiting pages cannot be freed quickly when memory
runs short.

pgfree_rcu in /proc/vmstat counts the deferred pages.  Nothing sets the
flag yet.

Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
[kas: rework for flagging at read time, 64-bit only and not PREEMPT_RT,
 shorter comments and changelog]
Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>

index 7a863572adce..a1e52a1f8a52 100644
--- a/include/linux/page-flags.h
+++ b/include/linux/page-flags.h
@@ -111,6 +111,9 @@ enum pageflags {
 	PG_swapbacked,		/* Page is backed by RAM/swap */
 	PG_unevictable,		/* Page is "unevictable"  */
 	PG_dropbehind,		/* drop pages on IO completion */
+#ifdef CONFIG_PAGE_RCU_FREE
+	PG_rcu_free,		/* free only after an RCU grace period */
+#endif
 #ifdef CONFIG_MMU
 	PG_mlocked,		/* Page is vma mlocked */
 #endif
@@ -602,6 +605,24 @@ FOLIO_FLAG(dropbehind, FOLIO_HEAD_PAGE)
 	FOLIO_TEST_CLEAR_FLAG(dropbehind, FOLIO_HEAD_PAGE)
 	__FOLIO_SET_FLAG(dropbehind, FOLIO_HEAD_PAGE)
 
+/*
+ * A lockless lookup that sees PG_rcu_free and then still finds the folio
+ * where it looked may read it until rcu_read_unlock().  Set under a
+ * reference, cleared only by the free.  Not for hugetlb or
+ * free_pages_nolock().
+ */

+FOLIO_TEST_FLAG(rcu_free, FOLIO_HEAD_PAGE)
+	FOLIO_TEST_SET_FLAG(rcu_free, FOLIO_HEAD_PAGE)
+	__FOLIO_CLEAR_FLAG(rcu_free, FOLIO_HEAD_PAGE)
+#define __PG_RCU_FREE (1UL << PG_rcu_free)
+#else
+FOLIO_TEST_FLAG_FALSE(rcu_free)
+	FOLIO_TEST_SET_FLAG_FALSE(rcu_free)
+	__FOLIO_CLEAR_FLAG_NOOP(rcu_free)
+#define __PG_RCU_FREE 0
+#endif

diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.c b/mm/page_alloc.c
index 12fac9084c48..a371e92da273 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.c
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.c
@@ -1313,6 +1313,96 @@ static inline void pgalloc_tag_sub_pages(struct alloc_tag *tag, unsigned int nr)
 
 #endif /* CONFIG_MEM_ALLOC_PROFILING */
 
+/*
+ * Each CPU has at most one grace period in flight (@queued), covering
+ * @batch.  Folios freed meanwhile wait on @pending for the next one.
+ */
+struct rcu_free_pcpu {
+	spinlock_t lock;
+	bool queued;
+	struct list_head pending;
+	struct list_head batch;
+	struct rcu_work rwork;
+};
+
+static DEFINE_PER_CPU(struct rcu_free_pcpu, rcu_free_pcpu);
+
+static struct workqueue_struct *rcu_free_wq __ro_after_init;
+
+static void rcu_free_start(struct rcu_free_pcpu *r)
+{
+	lockdep_assert_held(&r->lock);
+
+	if (r->queued || list_empty(&r->pending))
+		return;
+
+	list_splice_init(&r->pending, &r->batch);
+	r->queued = true;
+	WARN_ON_ONCE(!queue_rcu_work(rcu_free_wq, &r->rwork));
+}
+
+static void rcu_free_pages(struct list_head *list)
+{
+	struct folio_batch fbatch;
+	struct folio *folio, *next;
+
+	folio_batch_init(&fbatch);
+	list_for_each_entry_safe(folio, next, list, lru) {
+		if (!folio_batch_add(&fbatch, folio)) {
+			free_unref_folios(&fbatch);
+			cond_resched_tasks_rcu_qs();
+		}
+	}
+	if (folio_batch_count(&fbatch))
+		free_unref_folios(&fbatch);
+}
+
+static void rcu_free_workfn(struct work_struct *work)
+{
+	struct rcu_free_pcpu *r = container_of(to_rcu_work(work),
+					       struct rcu_free_pcpu, rwork);
+	LIST_HEAD(done);
+
+	spin_lock_irq(&r->lock);
+	list_splice_init(&r->batch, &done);
+	r->queued = false;
+	rcu_free_start(r);
+	spin_unlock_irq(&r->lock);
+
+	rcu_free_pages(&done);
+}
+
+static void rcu_free_defer(struct folio *folio)
+{
+	struct rcu_free_pcpu *r = raw_cpu_ptr(&rcu_free_pcpu);
+	unsigned long flags;
+
+	spin_lock_irqsave(&r->lock, flags);
+	list_add_tail(&folio->lru, &r->pending);
+	rcu_free_start(r);
+	spin_unlock_irqrestore(&r->lock, flags);
+}
+
+static void __init rcu_free_init(void)
+{
+	int cpu;
+
+	if (!IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PAGE_RCU_FREE))
+		return;
+
+	rcu_free_wq = alloc_workqueue("rcu_free",
+				      WQ_MEM_RECLAIM | WQ_PERCPU, 0);
+
+	for_each_possible_cpu(cpu) {
+		struct rcu_free_pcpu *r = per_cpu_ptr(&rcu_free_pcpu, cpu);
+
+		spin_lock_init(&r->lock);
+		INIT_LIST_HEAD(&r->pending);
+		INIT_LIST_HEAD(&r->batch);
+		INIT_RCU_WORK(&r->rwork, rcu_free_workfn);
+	}
+}
+

 		unsigned int order, fpi_t fpi_flags)
 {
@@ -1327,6 +1417,19 @@ static __always_inline bool __free_pages_prepare(struct page *page,
 
 	VM_BUG_ON_PAGE(PageTail(page), page);

+		VM_WARN_ON_ONCE(fpi_flags & FPI_NOLOCK);
+		__folio_clear_rcu_free(folio);
+		count_vm_events(PGFREE_RCU, 1 << order);
+		rcu_free_defer(folio);
+		return false;
+	}
+
 	trace_mm_page_free(page, order);
 	kmsan_free_page(page, order);
 
@@ -6401,6 +6504,8 @@ void __init setup_per_cpu_pageset(void)
 	for_each_online_pgdat(pgdat)
 		pgdat->per_cpu_nodestats =
 			alloc_percpu(struct per_cpu_nodestat);
+
+	rcu_free_init();
 }

From: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

PG_rcu_free holds back the reuse of a folio's memory until a grace
period after the folio is freed.  A stolen page cache pipe buffer is
reused without being freed: remove_mapping() takes the folio out of the
page cache and the caller keeps it.  fuse_try_move_folio() puts it into
a fuse file, where writes change it under a reader that found it before
the steal.

Drop ->try_steal from page_cache_pipe_buf_ops.  fuse_try_move_folio()
and virtio_console's pipe_to_sg() then copy, as they already do when
stealing fails.  SPLICE_F_MOVE from the page cache into a fuse file or
a virtio console now copies.

Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
[kas: rewrote the changelog]
Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>

 }
 
-/*
- * Attempt to steal a page from a pipe buffer. This should perhaps go into
- * a vm helper function, it's already simplified quite a bit by the
- * addition of remove_mapping(). If success is returned, the caller may
- * attempt to reuse this page for another destination.
- */
-static bool page_cache_pipe_buf_try_steal(struct pipe_inode_info *pipe,
-		struct pipe_buffer *buf)
-{
-	struct folio *folio = page_folio(buf->page);
-	struct address_space *mapping;
-
-	folio_lock(folio);
-
-	mapping = folio_mapping(folio);
-	if (mapping) {
-		WARN_ON(!folio_test_uptodate(folio));
-
-		/*
-		 * At least for ext2 with nobh option, we need to wait on
-		 * writeback completing on this folio, since we'll remove it
-		 * from the pagecache.  Otherwise truncate wont wait on the
-		 * folio, allowing the disk blocks to be reused by someone else
-		 * before we actually wrote our data to them. fs corruption
-		 * ensues.
-		 */
-		folio_wait_writeback(folio);
-
-		if (!filemap_release_folio(folio, GFP_KERNEL))
-			goto out_unlock;
-
-		/*
-		 * If we succeeded in removing the mapping, set LRU flag
-		 * and return good.
-		 */
-		if (remove_mapping(mapping, folio)) {
-			buf->flags |= PIPE_BUF_FLAG_LRU;
-			return true;
-		}
-	}
-
-	/*
-	 * Raced with truncate or failed to remove folio from current
-	 * address space, unlock and return failure.
-	 */
-out_unlock:
-	folio_unlock(folio);
-	return false;
-}

 					struct pipe_buffer *buf)

@@ -155,7 +105,6 @@ static int page_cache_pipe_buf_confirm(struct pipe_inode_info *pipe,

 	.confirm	= page_cache_pipe_buf_confirm,
 	.release	= page_cache_pipe_buf_release,
-	.try_steal	= page_cache_pipe_buf_try_steal,

fuse_try_move_folio() takes the folio of a pipe buffer and puts it into
a fuse file, where writes change it.  A folio with PG_rcu_free may still
be copied by a lockless page cache read that found it before it left
the page cache.

Such a folio reaches fuse when a mapped file page is gifted with
vmsplice(SPLICE_F_GIFT) and its file is then truncated.
fuse_check_folio() refuses it only because the flag is not among those
it allows, and with a dump_page().

Copy such a folio instead, as fuse does whenever it cannot take one.

Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>

 	newfolio = page_folio(buf->page);
 
+	/* A lockless page cache read may still be copying from it */
+	if (folio_test_rcu_free(newfolio))
+		goto out_fallback_unlock;
+
 	folio_clear_uptodate(newfolio);
 	folio_clear_mappedtodisk(newfolio);

Deferred folios have refcount 0 and are not on the free lists, so no
counter shows them.  Memory that waits for a grace period is missing
from the free count and from every LRU count.

Count it per zone in NR_FREE_RCU_PAGES: nr_free_rcu in /proc/vmstat,
free_rcu in show_free_areas().  Preparation for freeing the waiting
pages sooner when they hold back memory that is needed.

reviews.author: Kiryl (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern that the expedited grace period should only be triggered when memory is low, and explained how this is implemented by taking both CPU lists and freeing them after an expedited grace period when more than 4 MiB is pending on a CPU. The author also clarified that the expedited grace period interrupts every CPU and should be used sparingly.

reviews.author: Kiryl (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed David Hildenbrand's concern about removing ->try_steal from page_cache_pipe_buf_ops, explaining that fuse_try_move_folio() and virtio_console's pipe_to_sg() already copy the stolen page cache pipe buffer when stealing fails. The author confirmed this change is a simplification and does not have any significant performance impact.
reviews.raw_body:
A page whose free waits for an RCU grace period has refcount 0 and is
neither on the LRU nor in the buddy allocator.  memory_failure() and
soft_offline_page() cannot handle such a page: get_any_page() retries a
few times and gives up.  Soft offline of the page fails, and a hard
error is ignored.  If the page is part of a large folio, the folio is
later freed with the poisoned page in it, and that page can be handed
out again.

Free the waiting pages first when the page looks like one of them, and
again on each retry in get_any_page(): the page can be freed while it
retries.  memory_failure() has to do it before it sets PG_hwpoison.  The
free of a poisoned order-0 page drops the page instead of returning it
to the buddy allocator, so a later drain would still leave the error
ignored.

A folio with PG_rcu_free that is still in use may be copied by a reader
that holds no reference.  When memory_failure() succeeds, its caller can
unmap the page from the direct map under such a reader.  Wait for a
grace period before returning success.  By then the page has left the
page cache, or is an order-0 folio with PG_hwpoison, which a reader that
starts after the grace period has to check.

Wait at the end, not right after setting PG_hwpoison.  A large folio is
split later, and until the new folios are in the page cache, a reader
can still copy the poisoned page as part of the large one.

Both callers hold mf_mutex and can wait for the grace period.

Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
---
 mm/memory-failure.c | 29 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 29 insertions(+)

diff --git a/mm/memory-failure.c b/mm/memory-failure.c
index 7dde7c3c9a0c..398463b2e82d 100644
--- a/mm/memory-failure.c
+++ b/mm/memory-failure.c
@@ -1419,6 +1419,19 @@ static int __get_hwpoison_page(struct page *page, unsigned long flags)
 	return 0;
 }
 
+/* A page waiting for a grace period is not in the buddy yet: free it */
+static void mf_free_rcu_pages(struct page *p)
+{
+	if (!zone_rcu_free_waiting(page_zone(p)))
+		return;
+	if (page_count(p))
+		return;
+	if (is_free_buddy_page(p))
+		return;
+
+	rcu_free_sync();
+}
+
 #define GET_PAGE_MAX_RETRY_NUM 3
 
 static int get_any_page(struct page *p, unsigned long flags)
@@ -1443,6 +1456,7 @@ static int get_any_page(struct page *p, unsigned long flags)
 	}
 
 try_again:
+	mf_free_rcu_pages(p);
 	if (!count_increased) {
 		ret = __get_hwpoison_page(p, flags);
 		if (!ret) {
@@ -2440,6 +2454,7 @@ int memory_failure(unsigned long pfn, int flags)
 	if (res != -ENOENT)
 		goto unlock_mutex;
 
+	mf_free_rcu_pages(p);
 	if (TestSetPageHWPoison(p)) {
 		res = -EHWPOISON;
 		if (flags & MF_ACTION_REQUIRED)
@@ -2447,6 +2462,13 @@ int memory_failure(unsigned long pfn, int flags)
 		if (flags & MF_COUNT_INCREASED)
 			put_page(p);
 		action_result(pfn, MF_MSG_ALREADY_POISONED, MF_FAILED);
+		/*
+		 * The memory_failure() that set PG_hwpoison may have failed
+		 * without waiting for lockless readers, and the caller may
+		 * unmap the page once this returns 0.
+		 */
+		if (!res && folio_test_rcu_free(page_folio(p)))
+			synchronize_rcu();
 		goto unlock_mutex;
 	}
 
@@ -2612,6 +2634,13 @@ int memory_failure(unsigned long pfn, int flags)
 
 identify_page_state:
 	res = identify_page_state(pfn, p, page_flags);
+	/*
+	 * The caller may unmap the page once this returns 0.  Lockless
+	 * readers that started before the page got PG_hwpoison, or before a
+	 * split left it in a folio of its own, may still be copying it.
+	 */
+	if (!res && folio_test_rcu_free(folio))
+		synchronize_rcu();
 	mutex_unlock(&mf_mutex);
 	return res;
 unlock_page:

SPLICE_F_MOVE has not moved page cache folios between files since 2007.
See 485ddb4b9741 ("1/2 splice: dont steal").  The only users that still
steal from a pipe are fuse, when a server splices into /dev/fuse with
SPLICE_F_MOVE, and virtio_console's splice_write().  With this patch
both copy, and the source file keeps its folio cached.

Miklos, Bernd, Amit: do you know of users that depend on the move?  Would
the copy hurt them?

--

2026-11-04.patch_summary: This patch series proposes a change to how Linux handles page cache reads, allowing multiple CPUs to read from the same folio without taking a reference. This is done by introducing a new flag PG_rcu_free and deferring the freeing of folios until an RCU grace period. The goal is to reduce contention between readers and improve performance in scenarios where many threads are reading the same pages. The patch series includes 18 patches that implement this change, including modifications to filemap_read(), shmem, and other related functions.

reviews.summary: Reviewer Linus Torvalds expressed strong disagreement with Kiryl's patch, arguing that attempting to corral RCU freeing into a special case would make the code fragile and less useful, and instead suggested removing fuse_try_move_folio() entirely. He also proposed getting rid of pipe_buf_try_steal() and its associated functions.
reviews.raw_body:
On Mon, 9 Nov 2026 at 06:43, David Hildenbrand (Arm) <david@kernel.org> wrote:
>
> Can we just rework that code first to have some clear folio freeing path, IOW
> doing this in a folio-specific helper?

I think you're making things worse rather than better.

The whole point was to hook into *one* place: the page freeing.

Trying to make it specific to one special freeing path only makes it
fragile and less obvious, and results in anybody who then uses some
other freeing model to miss the RCU thing.

It also means that suddenly nobody else can use the RCU path for their own uses.

Look at all the kmalloc RCU freeing: it's used all over the place. RCU
has basically taken over the kernel. Every single performance-critical
lock-free area of the kernel wants RCU freeing.

I think trying to corral it into some special case is the last thing
we want to do. It only makes things less potentially useful and more
fragile.

                  Linus

---

On Mon, 9 Nov 2026 at 06:46, David Hildenbrand (Arm) <david@kernel.org> wrote:
>
> Could we get rid of fuse_try_move_folio() entirely?

Please. That would be great.

              Linus

---

On Mon, 9 Nov 2026 at 08:28, Linus Torvalds
<torvalds@linux-foundation.org> wrote:
>
> On Mon, 9 Nov 2026 at 06:46, David Hildenbrand (Arm) <david@kernel.org> wrote:
> >
> > Could we get rid of fuse_try_move_folio() entirely?
>
> Please. That would be great.

.. and in a similar vein, we should get rid of splice doing the same entirely.

Kirly's patch to just remove page_cache_pipe_buf_try_steal() entirely
(ok, it was originally mine, but Kiryl took ownership of that series:
"Tag, you're it") is worth doing, but I think worth doubling down on.
I think we sh ould just get rid of 'try_steal' entirely. I don't think
anybody really uses it. I think it exists in fuse and in the virtio
console, and neither is worth it.

Removing pipe_buf_try_steal() would basically remove all of
fuse_try_move_folio().

Conversely, removing fuse_try_move_folio() would make
pipe_buf_try_steal() even less useful than it is now.

Just remove them both. Good riddance.

                 Linus

---

On Mon, 9 Nov 2026 at 09:24, David Hildenbrand (Arm) <david@kernel.org> wrote:
> >
> > I think trying to corral it into some special case is the last thing
> > we want to do. It only makes things less potentially useful and more
> > fragile.
> Let me wrap my head around how this would look when we decouple pages from
> folios, where pages might not have a ->lru anymore, or not even a refcount.

So for an example of a place that already does RCU freeing of pages -
*not* folios - look at the TLB shootdown.

It's very round-about and hard to tell, but it's using

  tlb_remove_table_free
    call_rcu(&batch->rcu, tlb_remove_table_rcu);

and that then does

  tlb_remove_table_rcu ->
    __tlb_remove_table_free ->
      __tlb_remove_table ->
        pagetable_dtor_free ->
          pagetable_free ->
            __pagetable_free ->
               __free_pages(page, compound_order(page))

(and I might have messed this up - this really is a rats nest of
nested inline functions).

And in order to do this all, it sets up *another* page just to contain
the batching (which is also RCU-free'd)

Now, the batching is probably a very good thing in that context, so
I'm not actually suggesting this should be converted to some common
RCU-freeing thing.

Rather, I'm pointing out that we have existing hacks in this area that
have grown up over time and would have been a *lot* less hacky if we
had had a proper RCU-freeing page allocator back when that whole TLB
freeing code was written.

So I'm not saying "we should unify this". But I *am* saying "look, RCU
freeing of pages is _already_ a thing, and we have complicated hacky
things in place for it".

And they are complicated not because they necessarily should be
complicated, but because we solved the TLB shootdown after we already
had tons of complex architecture-specific code in place, and we
basically ended up adding that RCU phase on top of that existing
per-architecture complexity and abstraction.

*NOW* it would be actually fairly painful to try to convert the TLB
shootdown to a new order. But originally, it would have been very nice
if we had just had a "Oh, mark this page for RCU freeing".

(In all fairness, we also did it that way because some architectures
don't need the RCU delay simply because they have some other hardware
page walking infrastructure than the actual page tables the kernel
builds up. Not that those architectures *matter* today, but some of
that per-architecture inline function stuff is required to basically
isolate these kinds of decisions from the MM code - that deep inline
function indirection has a reason that is entirely independent of the
freeing side).

                    Linus

residing in a single physical page on some architectures (at least powerpc),
which makes using ptdesc / ->lru impossible as well, as we might only be freeing
parts of a page instead of full pages.

And some page tables today might already be allocated from slab (I think at
least sparc64 and m68k do that).

So that's one of the reason why tlb_remove_table() consumes a void * pointer
instead of a page/ptdesc pointer. It's all linked to
CONFIG_HAVE_ARCH_TLB_REMOVE_TABLE IIRC.

> freeing code was written.

See, I am not sure about that given the challenge with
CONFIG_HAVE_ARCH_TLB_REMOVE_TABLE. And apparently powerpc is using that, which
is not quite the museum piece (compared to m68k and sparc64 :) )

In a perfect world without these corner cases that make our life hard, possibly.

> 
> So I'm not saying "we should unify this". But I *am* saying "look, RCU
> freeing of pages is _already_ a thing, and we have complicated hacky
> things in place for it".
> 
> And they are complicated not because they necessarily should be
> complicated, but because we solved the TLB shootdown after we already
> had tons of complex architecture-specific code in place, and we
> basically ended up adding that RCU phase on top of that existing

Jup.

> 
> *NOW* it would be actually fairly painful to try to convert the TLB
> shootdown to a new order. But originally, it would have been very nice

> that per-architecture inline function stuff is required to basically
> isolate these kinds of decisions from the MM code - that deep inline
> function indirection has a reason that is entirely independent of the
> freeing side).

There are some dirty details when it comes to the upcoming page vs. folio split
that I am still unclear about.

The page table example you mention above is another prime example of the
challenges we'll face: page tables will have a separately allocated memdesc
("ptdesc"), just like folios will have their memdesc ("folio") separately allocated.

When RCU freeing, we'll really have to keep the allocated memdesc alive as well.
RCU-freeing the page only is not sufficient.

There was even talk about allocating page tables from slab later, as long as we
can adjust a "struct ptdesc" to it. Which would solve the problem of powerpc
etc. that don't operate on full pages for page tables.

So I might be completely off, but what I imagine is that the memdescs will get
RCU-freed (these are not pages), and once they are then getting freed, they will
probably take the physical page with them.

And freeing memdescs through RCU will likely be memdesc specific.

I really don't know, Willy might know more about these plans.

But I am overloaded with all the Fixes, so my brain doesn't work quite right.

-- 
Cheers,

David

> Right: once the folio is allocated separately, the lockless read
> dereferences it too, so it has to wait for the grace period along with

> 
> Until then the folio is the struct page, and __free_pages_prepare() is

If we go that way, don't make it effectively folio-centric in the
